title: Check yourself: Audit the sessions, order the fixes and the practice

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: After a change that made the agent escalate less, first-contact resolution rose from 0.60 to 0.75 and the team reports success. What does the audit still have to show?

options.text: That tokens per conversation fell by the same proportion as the escalation rate
options.says: Ruled out because tokens are not what the change risked: "Both are visible only against labels."

options.text: That sessions settled alone although a human was needed did not increase
options.says: A lower escalation rate is a success only if no case that needed a person was settled alone.

options.text: That the prompt now holds fewer words than before the change was made
options.says: Ruled out because the length of a prompt is not the risk: "A rate alone is a bad objective".

options.text: That the confidence scores of the model moved up together with the rate
options.says: Ruled out because a number the model reports is unmeasured: "The course treats the number as a claim that has to be measured against labelled outcomes before anything is routed on it".

questions.stem: One session holds eleven calls to the wrong tool, and the audit reports a count of one for the wrong-tool shape. A manager asks why not eleven. What is the answer?

options.text: The audit keeps only the first mistake of each session in the report
options.says: Ruled out because the audit does not drop later mistakes for space: "The count of steps is still a useful diagnostic for a single session."

options.text: Counts are capped at one by default, whatever the session holds
options.says: Ruled out because nothing in the audit caps a count: "The audit counts each failure shape once per session."

options.text: The other ten calls were retries, which the audit leaves out
options.says: Ruled out because every call was a pick of the wrong tool and none is set aside: "A conversation in which the model picked the wrong tool eleven times is one failed conversation".

options.text: The target is a share of conversations, and each fails at most once
options.says: The unit of the target is the conversation.

questions.stem: The audit needs two fields for each session: whether a human was needed, and which tool each step should have used. Which source supplies them?

options.text: The tool logs, which record every call with its arguments and its result
options.says: Ruled out because the logs hold the calls and not the judgements: "Two fields are not."

options.text: Reviewers who label a sample of the sessions by hand
options.says: A judgement about need and about the right tool is made by a person, on a sample.

options.text: The model, which can be asked after each conversation to mark its own errors
options.says: Ruled out because the audit exists to check the agent against something other than itself: "a number computed only on what is easy to read is flattering".

options.text: The customer, through a short survey sent at the end of each conversation
options.says: Ruled out because a survey does not say which tool was right: "Whether a case needed a person is a judgement, and so is which tool a step should have used."

origin.section: What the logs hold and what a person has to label
